subsystems.name: Quantum transducer
subsystems.role: the physical system whose quantum state is measured; different systems suit different quantities (time, magnetic field, acceleration).

subsystems.name: State preparation
subsystems.role: initialises the transducer into a known quantum state.
parts: laser systems for cooling and optical pumping

subsystems.name: Control and manipulation
subsystems.role: applies precise pulses or fields to make the quantum state evolve in response to the quantity being sensed.

subsystems.name: Isolation and shielding
subsystems.role: protects the fragile quantum state from thermal, magnetic and vibrational noise.

subsystems.name: Readout
subsystems.role: converts the final quantum state into a measurable signal.

subsystems.name: Signal processing and stabilisation
subsystems.role: extracts the measurement and locks the sensor to a reference to reduce drift.

buildSteps.title: Choose the quantum system
buildSteps.detail: Select atoms, defects or photons whose energy levels respond to the target quantity — time, magnetic field, gravity or acceleration.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the sensor head
buildSteps.detail: For an atomic sensor, build a vacuum cell or chip-scale trap; for a diamond magnetometer, grow diamond and engineer nitrogen-vacancy centres near the surface.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the quantum state
buildSteps.detail: Use lasers to cool atoms or optically pump spins into a known state, often requiring a vacuum or a cryogenic environment.

buildSteps.title: Isolate from noise
buildSteps.detail: Enclose the sensor in magnetic shielding, vibration isolation and temperature control so external disturbances do not swamp the signal.

buildSteps.title: Manipulate the state
buildSteps.detail: Apply microwave, radio-frequency or optical pulses — or let the state evolve freely — so it accumulates a phase or population difference proportional to the measured quantity.

buildSteps.title: Read out the result
buildSteps.detail: Measure fluorescence, absorption or interference fringes with photodetectors, converting the quantum phase into an electrical signal.

buildSteps.title: Stabilise and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Lock the sensor to a stable reference (for clocks, a primary frequency standard) and correct for drifts, temperature and ageing.

buildSteps.title: Package and ruggedise
buildSteps.detail: Miniaturise optics, electronics and shielding into a field-deployable unit, often using photonic integrated circuits and chip-scale vacuum cells.

buildSteps.title: Validate in the field
buildSteps.detail: Compare against conventional instruments and run long-duration tests in the intended environment — a ship, aircraft, hospital or survey vehicle.

prerequisites.why: needed to cool, trap and read out atoms and to manipulate spins.
many quantum states survive only in ultra-high vacuum or at low temperature.
precise pulses and fields control the quantum state and define measurement sequences.
high-quality nitrogen-vacancy centres are made today, but wafer-scale reproducible fabrication is still maturing.
used in gravitational-wave detectors to beat the standard quantum limit; broader commercial deployment is emerging.

pathway.milestone: commercial atomic clocks, magnetometers, gravimeters and squeezed-light-enhanced interferometers
pathway.unlocks: better timekeeping, geophysical surveys, navigation and gravitational-wave astronomy.

pathway.milestone: chip-scale and cold-atom inertial sensors for GPS-denied navigation
pathway.unlocks: robust positioning for ships, aircraft and underground or underwater vehicles without satellite signals.

pathway.milestone: medical imaging with quantum magnetometers, such as nitrogen-vacancy magnetoencephalography
pathway.unlocks: wearable brain imaging and more sensitive diagnostic tools.
distributed sensing for fundamental physics — dark matter searches, gravity mapping and improved radar or LiDAR.
